decision: how the row's lagging state is stored
choice: derived from job_events (preflight-lagging, requeued-lagging, bounded by the last run-died or run-exited); no new column or table
why: no schema change; the same events show in history
the repo's only deploy timeout: health already flags a device lagging or deploying that long; the job timeout (60 min) was the rejected alternative, a later alarm
a deploy normally lands within one heal cycle; the short first step lets the job start soon after the checkout catches up

choice: the box's own device_sync row when the box lags origin/main, whichever device the job was placed on
why: the box lag blocks every device; marking the placed remote let heal flip it back to synced and the next claim refused at once

choice: tests/test_lagging_requeue.py drives the real waiter preflight against a git checkout behind origin/main and the real dispatcher T6 on a fake clock
why: each acceptance criterion is a test; with lib/waiter.py reverted to main, the ac-1 and ac-3 tests fail (queued instead of failed)

decision: round 1 f-1: a lagging review of a replaced head
choice: _lagging_handled runs _review_retry_waits before both its requeue and its device-lagging stuck
why: the rule is #71's: a failed review of a replaced head is never retried; the link-drop and attempt-1 paths already ran that guard, the lagging path skipped it

decision: round 1 f-2: who a ready is charged to after a lagging refusal
choice: _update_job_before counts a row whose latest end is preflight-lagging as never started, beside failed-unstarted
why: the rule is #241's: a ready is charged only to an update whose worker started; a lagging refusal frees the slot before any worker runs, so the failed row no longer carries a placement

decision: round 2 f-3: a job queued behind a lagging checkout
choice: a queued row whose latest end is requeued-lagging, its harness sync-blocked on every device and its first refusal past the bound, is failed again as lag-blocked for T6 to stick
why: the rule is ac-3's: lag that persists past the bound escalates; a sync-blocked row is never claimed, so it is never refused again and T6, which reads only failed rows, never saw it

decision: round 2 f-4: a checkout that recovered during the last backoff
choice: T6 sticks device-lagging only when the lag is still seen past the bound (a refusal or lag-blocked that late, or every checkout for the harness lagging now), never from the first refusal's age alone
why: the rule is ac-2's: a recovered checkout starts the same job with no manual step; the age of an old refusal is not evidence the checkout still lags

decision: round 3 f-4: one checkout recovered, another refused after the bound
choice: T6 sticks device-lagging only when the job's harness is lag-blocked past the bound: every eligible device sync-blocked, or the box's own checkout lagging origin/main (it refuses every placement); a late refusal alone no longer sticks
why: the rule is ac-2's: a refusal proves only that the refusing checkout lags, so a recovered eligible checkout must get the retry; escalation needs every eligible checkout lagging
